answer: Reef Kernel Anchoring. Each agent’s reachable neighbor set must contain a kernel of peers that independently place it near the reef of the live graph—dense, low-churn zones. Placement requires reciprocal routing traffic from distinct existing clusters. To anchor a sybil near that zenith, an attacker must sustain real traffic and co-presence across many clusters, paying bandwidth, latency, and maintenance per identity, not a one-time fee.
